quests.instruction: The school bell rings at 8:00. Imran got there at 7:40, so he was early. Maya walked in at 8:15, so she was…
quests.hint: Compare when each child arrived with when the bell rang.
quests.explanation: Early means before the expected time. Late means after it.
quests.funFact: Many people feel sleepiest in the middle of the afternoon, which is perfectly normal.

quests.instruction: Mum says, “Wash your hands before you eat.” Which word completes: “Brush your teeth ___ you eat.”?
quests.hint: When does toothpaste make sense: with the meal, or once it’s finished?
quests.explanation: Before and after tell us the order things happen. Here, eating comes first and tooth-brushing follows.
quests.funFact: Dentists suggest brushing twice a day, in the morning and at night.

quests.instruction: In a relay race, the runner who starts is the first runner. The one who crosses the finish line carrying the baton is the…
quests.hint: Which runner’s turn comes at the very end?
quests.explanation: First means number one in order. Last means the final one, with nobody after.
quests.funFact: The final runner in a relay is often called the anchor.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “always”? (the sun rising every morning vs. snow falling in the desert at noon)
quests.hint: Which word means “not even once”?
quests.explanation: Always means every single time. Never means not a single time.
quests.funFact: Near the poles, the Sun can stay above the horizon for weeks in summer.

quests.instruction: Ravi plays cricket almost every day, so he plays often. He goes swimming just once or twice a year, so he swims…
quests.hint: Think of something that happens only once in a blue moon.
quests.explanation: Often means many times. Rarely means very few times.
quests.funFact: Leap years add an extra day, February 29, only about once every four years.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “morning”? (breakfast and sunrise vs. dinner and sunset)
quests.hint: When do most families sit down to dinner?
quests.explanation: Morning is the start of the day. Evening is the part when the day winds down.
quests.funFact: The word “morning” comes from “morn”, an old word for the early part of the day.

quests.instruction: Many English fairy tales open with “Once upon a time”. The part that finishes with “happily ever after” is the…
quests.hint: Which part of the story do you reach on the last page?
quests.explanation: The beginning starts a story. The ending wraps it up.
quests.funFact: Many fairy tales in English start with “Once upon a time”.

quests.instruction: The tent at the campsite is temporary; we’ll take it down on Sunday. The house we live in all year is…
quests.hint: Think of a home that stays put for years and years.
quests.explanation: Temporary things last only for a short time. Permanent things are meant to stay.
quests.funFact: Hermit crabs change shells as they grow, because a shell isn’t a permanent home for them.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “yesterday”? (the day that just ended vs. the day that’s about to begin)
quests.hint: If today is Wednesday, what day is Thursday?
quests.explanation: Yesterday is the day before today. Tomorrow is the day after today.
quests.funFact: The International Date Line is where one calendar day turns into the next.

quests.instruction: Dinosaurs lived in the distant past. A robot that might one day tidy your room belongs to the…
quests.hint: Which time has not happened yet?
quests.explanation: The past is everything that has already happened. The future is everything still to come.
quests.funFact: Dinosaurs lived millions of years ago, long before there were any people.

quests.instruction: The sun is highest overhead around noon. Twelve hours later, when it’s the deep middle of the night, the clock says…
quests.hint: From lunchtime, count twelve hours forward.
quests.explanation: Noon is twelve o’clock in the middle of the day. Midnight is twelve o’clock in the middle of the night.
quests.funFact: “a.m.” and “p.m.” come from Latin phrases meaning before and after midday.

quests.instruction: At new moon, the Moon is almost impossible to see. About two weeks later, it looks like a bright, round plate: the…
quests.hint: Which phase fills the whole circle with light?
quests.explanation: A new moon shows hardly any lit surface from Earth. A full moon shows all of it.
quests.funFact: The Moon takes about 29 and a half days to go from one new moon to the next.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “brief”? (a five-minute chat in the corridor vs. a three-hour speech)
quests.hint: Which would make you glance at the clock again and again?
quests.explanation: Brief means short in time. Lengthy means taking a long time.
quests.funFact: Some train journeys, like the Trans-Siberian railway, last about a week.

quests.instruction: The class trip bus was meant to arrive at 10:00, but traffic held it up and it pulled in at 10:45. It was…
quests.hint: A bus that reaches its stop later than planned has a word for that.
quests.explanation: Behind schedule means later than planned. Ahead of schedule means earlier than planned.
quests.funFact: “Schedule” comes from a Latin word for a small slip of paper.

quests.instruction: Aman is reading page 12. The page he just finished is the previous page. The one he’ll turn to is the…
quests.hint: Which page comes right after the one in front of you?
quests.explanation: Previous means coming just before. Next means coming just after.
quests.funFact: The Gutenberg Bible was printed in the 1450s, one of the first big books printed with movable metal type.

quests.instruction: Neel gets up at 6:30 every school day. At nine each night, he…
quests.hint: What does he do at the end of every evening?
quests.explanation: Getting up starts your day. Going to bed ends it.
quests.funFact: Sleep helps your brain sort out what you learned during the day.

quests.instruction: Before dinner, Dina sets the table with plates and spoons. When everyone has finished eating, her brother…
quests.hint: Between the meal and the washing-up, there is one more job.
quests.explanation: Setting the table puts everything out before the meal. Clearing it takes everything away afterward.
quests.funFact: Chopsticks have been used in China for thousands of years.

quests.instruction: The first show starts at 4:00 and the second at 6:00. The second show begins…
quests.hint: Which clock time is further along in the day?
quests.explanation: Earlier means closer to the start of the day. Later means further from it.
quests.funFact: The first public movie screening took place in Paris in 1895.

quests.instruction: Mum’s calendar for Saturday is crammed with errands, so she’s busy. Sunday has nothing planned, so she’s…
quests.hint: Which day has space for a long walk?
quests.explanation: Busy means your time is taken up with things to do. Free means you have nothing planned.
quests.funFact: The word “free” can also mean “costs nothing”.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “term time”? (school days with lessons vs. weeks with no school)
quests.hint: The weeks when you can sleep in have a name.
quests.explanation: Term time is when school is in session. A holiday is a break from it.
quests.funFact: The word “holiday” comes from “holy day”.

quests.instruction: Spring is when many trees sprout new leaves. In the opposite season, autumn, many of those same trees…
quests.hint: What happens to leaves before winter arrives?
quests.explanation: Spring is the season of new growth. Autumn is the season when growth slows and many leaves fall.
quests.funFact: In American English, autumn is often called “fall” because leaves fall from the trees.

quests.instruction: The school bus comes at exactly 7:30 every morning, which is regular. A bus that turns up sometimes at 7, sometimes at 8 and sometimes not at all is…
quests.hint: Can you set your watch by it?
quests.explanation: Regular means happening in a steady pattern. Irregular means there’s no reliable pattern.
quests.funFact: A healthy heart beats in a steady, regular rhythm.

quests.instruction: Rina’s model volcano is still being built, so the project is ongoing. When she adds the last splash of paint, it will be…
quests.hint: Think about a project where nothing is left to do.
quests.explanation: Ongoing means still happening. Completed means finished.
quests.funFact: Mount Etna in Sicily is one of the most active volcanoes in the world.

quests.instruction: Zia packed her bag, checked the timetable and put on her coat, so she was prepared. Her brother dashed out without his lunch or his book. He was…
quests.hint: Who has everything they’ll need for the day?
quests.explanation: Prepared means ready for what’s coming. Unprepared means not ready.
quests.funFact: The Scout motto is “Be prepared”.

quests.instruction: Heavy rain meant the match couldn’t be played on Saturday, so the coach postponed it. If the sun came out and the teams wanted to play sooner, they could…
quests.hint: Which direction does the date move when you make something happen earlier?
quests.explanation: To postpone is to move something to a later time. To bring it forward is to move it to an earlier time.
quests.funFact: Cricket matches are often paused for rain, and the players come back when it clears.

quests.instruction: Tara checks the clock constantly, every minute or so. Her brother only glances at it…
quests.hint: Picture someone glancing at the clock only now and then.
quests.explanation: Constantly means again and again without a break. Occasionally means now and then.
quests.funFact: A day has 86,400 seconds.

quests.instruction: The school painted its gate last month, so that happened recently. The school building itself went up in 1920, which was…
quests.hint: Which one did people do before your grandparents were born?
quests.explanation: Recently means not long before now. Long ago means far back in the past.
quests.funFact: Some schools in India have been open for more than a hundred years.

quests.instruction: The teacher asks, “Have you finished your drawing?” Isha has colored every part and says, “Yes, I’m done already.” Kabir has only sketched the outline, so he says…
quests.hint: Which answer means “I’ll finish, but later”?
quests.explanation: Already means something has happened before now. Not yet means it hasn’t happened, but it may soon.
quests.funFact: “Already” is one word, but “all ready” is two, and they mean different things.

quests.instruction: Which word describes the opposite of “peak time” on a train? (everyone heading to work at 8 a.m. vs. the quiet stretch at 11 a.m.)
quests.hint: Think of the time of day when you’d find an empty seat.
quests.explanation: Peak times are when most people travel. Off-peak times are the quieter hours in between.
quests.funFact: Some train tickets cost less outside rush hours to encourage people to travel at quieter times.

quests.instruction: The Hegde family goes away on holiday every December. At the end of the trip, they…
quests.hint: What do travelers do after they reach home?
quests.explanation: Going away means leaving. Coming back means returning to where you started.
quests.funFact: Many birds fly away from cold places in winter and come back in spring.
